Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and intermittent headaches
radiating from the potserior cervical region. The reported mechnaism of injury is consistent with the forces involved in this type
of impact, and the presentation reflects a typical cervical strain pattern. Over the course of care, the patient attended 42 visits
consisting of manual therapy, supervised range-of-motion exercises, and home stretching instruction. Treatment followed a
conventional progression, with visit frequency tapering as symptoms improved and range of motion returned toward baseline.
Examination findings included reduced cervical roattion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, which support the diagnosis, while
neurological screening, reflexes, and strength testing remained within normal limits. No prior injury to the cervical spine or
surrounding soft tissue is known to this provider. Billing records reflect single entries for each service rendered, with no repeated
or duplicate charges. Prognosis is good with continued home exercise, and discharge from active care is anticipated.
